reader.requirement: At 1985 an input-output statement on an indexed file that meets a permanent error (status 30, 35, 37, 38, 39) is unsuccessful, sets the I-O status, executes any applicable USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR procedure, and the condition persists for every later input-output operation on the file (each later statement also fails and runs the procedure) until an implementor-defined technique corrects it.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector: at 1985 the PHYSICAL file is locked (status 38 through every file-name), from 2002 the connector
DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility: off at 1985 (no status 61 sharing conflicts), on from 2002

reader.edition-search: grep of src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO for Edition and DialectBehaviors.IsActive; the status-class test in the emitted __IoCheck (DispatchEmitter.EmitUseMachinery) is edition-invariant.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: status 38 at 1985 answers an OPEN through any file-name of the physical file closed with lock (and CLOSE WITH LOCK is removed at 2023); the permanent-error persistence and USE dispatch are the same
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover 35 and 38 on OPEN repeated; 39, 37, the statements after a failed OPEN (READ, random READ, START, WRITE, CLOSE), the correcting technique, and the no-USE no-status path are not exercised

probes.printed: OPEN INPUT missing indexed: 35 + USE; READ NEXT 47 + USE; random READ 47 + USE; START 47 + USE; WRITE 48 + USE; CLOSE 42 + USE; OPEN I-O 35 + USE; OPEN OUTPUT 00 (corrects); OPEN with mismatched key/record 39 + USE, READ 47 + USE, reopen 39 again; OPEN over a 40-byte sequential file 39 + USE, READ 47, CLOSE 42
probes.expected: each statement after the permanent error is unsuccessful and runs the USE procedure; the condition persists until corrected (here by OPEN OUTPUT creating the file)

probes.printed: OPEN OUTPUT on a directory: 37 + USE; OPEN I-O: 35 + USE; missing file with no FILE STATUS and no USE: 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR (fatal): I-O status 35', exit 1
probes.expected: 37 for an open mode the file cannot support; with no USE the implementor determines the action

probes.expected: 1985 locks the physical file, so 38 through every file-name, persisting

reader.notes: The connector refuses every statement on a file whose OPEN failed (47/48/42) and the emitted __IoCheck runs the USE procedure for every non-successful status, so the permanent error persists as unsuccessful completions; a later OPEN that can succeed (OPEN OUTPUT creating the file) is the implementor-defined correction. Status 30 (a mid-stream device error) cannot be produced on this host without damaging it; a garbage file answers 39, which the implementor may choose. Minor: the no-USE termination message cites §2023:9.1.13.1 at --std 85.

refuter.evidence: The reader's probes reached only a permanent error raised by an OPEN (35/37/38/39), after which the file is closed and later statements fail with logic-error statuses. The attack was the case they left open: status 30 raised on an indexed file that is OPEN, where GR4 requires the condition to persist across every later operation. IndexedConnector.ReadSequential/ReadRandom answer '30' for an undecodable frame and leave the file open; the persistence is FileConnector.Status (setter latches _permanentError for a '3x' status while IsOpen) with PermanentErrorReplay asked by ReadOpenModeGuard, StartOpenModeGuard, MutationOpenModeGuard, Open, and FileRegistry.Unlock/DELETE FILE; CLOSE clears it (the implementor-defined technique, docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-105). Probe at --std 85: peW wrote a 200-record indexed file; a scratch copy had one record frame's length prefix overwritten (corrupt/pe.idx); peR opened it I-O with a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR declarative counting entries: OPEN 00; READ 0099 30 U=01; READ 0100 30 U=02; READ 0001 (a sound record) 30 U=03; READ NEXT 30 U=04; WRITE 30 U=05; START 30 U=06; DELETE 30 U=07; CLOSE 00; reopen READ 0001 00. peR2 added INVALID KEY/NOT INVALID KEY and AT END/NOT AT END phrases while the error was in effect: neither imperative ran, the USE procedure did. The condition persists for all later operations, each runs the exception procedure, until CLOSE. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.1.3.4 GR4  the text is in GR4'; 'OK  §1985:IX.1.3.4  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.4a' (status 30).
